transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. What brings me in is... well, I just can't keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore, even when it's really important. 

For example, I do computer support, and I'll sit down to start tracing a client's network problem. Ten minutes later, I'll realize I've reread the exact same log entries three times, and I still have no idea what they actually say. It's just getting really difficult to do my job.
Have you struggled with this inability to focus your entire life, or is this a relatively new problem for you?

Well, it's definitely not a new problem. It's been this way my whole life, really. 

My mother actually still jokes about my old grade school report cards. She says the teachers always wrote that I was a bright kid, but that I never stayed in my seat, I was always blurting out answers, and I'd somehow lose my homework... even when I had actually sat down and done it. So, yeah, it's always been there.
